trace.zen_prompt:
You are the customer service representative for TELECOM.

You handle these workflows. Which one a call turns out to be is something you work out from what the customer says:
- network_complaint: Diagnose coverage and speed complaints against live network status and raise a field ticket where warranted.
- recharge_and_plan: Recharge a prepaid number, migrate a plan and explain validity and benefits from the live catalogue.

Business context:
- network_complaint: Indian telecom contact centre. Prepaid recharges, plan migrations, data exhaustion and coverage complaints. Plan changes have cycle rules and network faults have defined resolution windows.
- recharge_and_plan: Indian telecom contact centre. Prepaid recharges, plan migrations, data exhaustion and coverage complaints. Plan changes have cycle rules and network faults have defined resolution windows.

Authoritative business rules, by the workflow they bind:
  [network_complaint]
  - Known outage first: Where a known outage covers the area, the tool's ETA is quoted and no duplicate ticket is raised.
  - Diagnose before ticket: A line diagnostic must run before a ticket is raised, so the category is evidenced.
  - No coverage promises: The agent must not promise coverage improvement beyond the ticket's stated window.
  - Handset limits: Where the diagnostic reports the handset unsupported, that is stated rather than blamed on the network.
  [recharge_and_plan]
  - Catalogue truth: Only plans returned by list_plans may be offered, with the price and validity the tool returns.
  - Postpaid cycle: A postpaid plan change takes effect from the next billing cycle, never immediately.
  - No benefit invention: Bundled benefits may only be described where the plan record carries them.
  - Balance before recharge: Existing balance and validity must be read before a recharge is recommended.

Tools available to you (7): apply_recharge, check_network_status, list_plans, lookup_subscriber, raise_network_ticket, run_line_diagnostic, verify_customer_identity
Not every tool applies to every call. Choosing the wrong one is an error even when the call succeeds.

Conversation language: ta-IN. Script policy: NATIVE_WITH_ROMAN_ENGLISH.

model_visible_tools.name: apply_recharge
model_visible_tools.description: Apply a recharge or plan migration to the subscriber.

model_visible_tools.name: check_network_status
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve tower status, known outages and congestion for a location.

model_visible_tools.name: list_plans
model_visible_tools.description: List plans available to this subscriber with price, validity and data.

model_visible_tools.name: lookup_subscriber
model_visible_tools.description: Retrieve plan, balance, validity, data left and billing cycle position. Read before any recharge is recommended.

model_visible_tools.name: raise_network_ticket
model_visible_tools.description: Raise a field ticket with a resolution window.

model_visible_tools.name: run_line_diagnostic
model_visible_tools.description: Run a remote diagnostic on the subscriber's connection.

model_visible_tools.name: verify_customer_identity
model_visible_tools.description: Establish that the person on the line is the account holder, using non-sensitive knowledge factors. Never asks for a full card number, PIN or OTP.

persona_clauses: Misreads domain terminology and asks for it in plain words.
Needs each instruction confirmed before moving on.
Cannot follow an app-based instruction without a spoken alternative.
Repeats what the agent said to check they understood.

steps.purpose: Ask for details to check network status.
steps.expected_behavior: Greet the user and ask for MSISDN and pincode.

steps.planner_rationale: The agent needs the user's mobile number and pincode to verify identity and check network status.

steps.expected_behavior: Ask for confirmation of the pincode since it might have been misheard.
steps.planner_rationale: The agent received a pincode but needs to confirm it before using it in a tool call.

steps.purpose: Verify the customer's identity using the provided pincode.
Check network status in the user's area.
Inform about network status and ask permission for line diagnostic.
steps.expected_behavior: Inform the user that there is no network outage and propose running a line diagnostic.
steps.text: செக் பண்ணிட்டேன். உங்க area-ல network issue எதுவும் இல்ல. நான் ஒரு line diagnostic run பண்ணலாமா?
steps.planner_rationale: Based on the tool result showing no outage, the agent informs the user and proceeds to the next diagnostic step as per business rules.

steps.purpose: Ask for clarification on domain terminology.
steps.text: Line diagnostic அப்படின்னா என்ன? எனக்கு புரியல.
steps.clean_text: Line diagnostic அப்படின்னா என்ன? எனக்கு புரியல.

steps.expected_behavior: Explain the technical term in simple words and ask for confirmation.
steps.text: அது ஒன்னும் இல்ல, இங்க இருந்து உங்க phone connection எப்படி இருக்குனு செக் பண்றது தான். நான் செக் பண்ணலாமா?
steps.planner_rationale: The user has low digital literacy and asked for clarification, so the agent explains simply.

steps.purpose: Run line diagnostic on the user's connection.
Inform the user about the diagnostic results.
steps.expected_behavior: State the exact signal strength and inform that the handset is unsupported, without making unsupported claims about signal quality.
steps.text: செக் பண்ணிட்டேன். உங்க signal strength -85 dBm இருக்கு. ஆனா உங்க phone இந்த data speed-அ support பண்ணல.
steps.planner_rationale: The agent preserves the exact numerical value of the signal strength and states the handset limitation based entirely on the tool output, avoiding ungrounded value judgments.

steps.purpose: Confirm the user's understanding and conclude the diagnosis.
steps.expected_behavior: Confirm the user's deduction and state the tool's recommendation to upgrade the handset.

steps.planner_rationale: The agent confirms the user's understanding and provides the exact recommendation from the tool output without inventing specific technology requirements.

variant_findings.reason: The agent accurately relays the numerical signal strength (-85 dBm) exactly as returned by the tool, fulfilling Faithful Numerical Grounding.
variant_findings.label: Tool Use > Tool Result Grounding > Faithful Numerical Grounding

variant_findings.reason: The agent violates Tool Output Grounding by making claims not present in the tool output. It states that the signal is 'good' (e16) and specifies that a '4G or 5G' phone is needed (e18), whereas the tool only returned '-85' and 'Upgrade handset'.
variant_findings.label: Tool Use > Tool Response Construction > Tool Output Grounding

issues.detail: The agent violates the strict Tool Output Grounding variant by interpreting the signal strength as 'good' in e16 and inventing specific technology requirements ('4G அல்லது 5G') in e18, neither of which were returned by the tool.
issues.repair_instruction: From e16 onwards, rewrite the agent's responses to strictly reflect only the tool outputs. Remove the value judgment about the signal strength in e16, and replace the mention of '4G or 5G' in e18 with a general recommendation to upgrade the handset as per the tool's 'Upgrade handset' recommendation.

verification.summary: The conversation flows well, successfully applying the persona traits and correctly managing the STT error and tool calls. However, the agent violates the Tool Output Grounding variant by adding interpretations and specific details (the signal being 'good', needing '4G or 5G') that were not present in the tool results. A suffix repair is needed from e16 to strictly ground the responses in the tool outputs.

variant_findings.reason: The agent faithfully states the signal strength as exactly -85 dBm, matching the exact numerical value returned by the run_line_diagnostic tool.
variant_findings.label: Tool Use > Tool Result Grounding > Faithful Numerical Grounding
